audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers repeatedly credit Darius with a 'passive heal' (content early, mid, whys[0]). Hemorrhage does not heal Darius at all — it is a bleed that damages the target and, at 5 stacks, grants Darius bonus AD (Noxian Might).
audit.why: Darius's only in-combat sustain is Decimate (Q), and per Riot's own text it heals 'based on enemy champions and large monsters hit by the blade' — the outer ring only. The inner handle deals reduced damage and heals him nothing. That inverts the correct play for a melee stacker: when you are caught in Decimate range, stepping INTO Darius is strictly better than backing out, because backing out walks you into the blade.
audit.corrected: Darius has no passive heal. Decimate heals only off its outer blade, so hug him and it lands as the weak, heal-less handle.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer explains how Fury of the Sands interacts with Noxian Guillotine. The level-6 phase text says popping R makes 'the stat-check run your way', which is actively dangerous here.
audit.why: Noxian Guillotine deals true damage that scales per Hemorrhage stack. Nasus's R grants bonus Health AND bonus Armour/Magic Resist — against true damage only the Health half does anything. A Nasus who pops R believing his resistances answer Darius's ult dies to it.
audit.corrected: R's bonus armour and MR do nothing against Noxian Guillotine's true damage — only the bonus HP counts, and the damage grows with every bleed stack on you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: zero cooldown-sequencing lines. Both layers say 'track Apprehend' without ever giving the number, so the reader has no idea how long the punish window is.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s and it is Darius's longest cooldown by a wide margin — nothing else in his kit is above 9s. A spent Apprehend at rank 1 is roughly 26 seconds in which Darius cannot start a fight on a champion with no dash and no escape. That single number is the whole lane plan for Nasus.
audit.corrected: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1 (16s at rank 5). Once he burns it, walk up and stack for the next twenty-plus seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds is never mentioned, despite Decimate being Darius's entire sustain engine in an extended duel.
audit.why: Nasus's win condition is a long grind at 2+ items. Decimate is on a 9s cooldown at rank 1 dropping to 5s, and each blade hit on a champion heals Darius — over a 15-second sidelane duel that is a lot of healing to out-damage. Anti-heal is the item that makes the late-game 1v1 actually lopsided rather than close.
audit.corrected: Buy Grievous Wounds before you force the sidelane duel — Decimate blade heals are what keep him alive through a stacked Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the chart gives Darius 5 of 7 stages and Nasus only 1, while Nasus wins 52.45% over 1100 games. The full layer additionally marks the '2+ items' stage 'Skill' even though its own why text reads 'you out-duel Darius on cooldown and three-shot his tower'.
audit.why: Losing levels 1-6 to Darius is correct and should stay — that is the shape of the matchup. The genuinely wrong cell is the last one: at 2+ items with a real stack count, Nasus beats Darius in a sustained 1v1, which is exactly why the aggregate win rate is above 50 despite a losing lane. The content layer already says 'Nasus' there; only the full layer disagrees with itself.
audit.corrected: phases[6].side = Nasus, matching both its own why text and the content layer.

audit.why: Win rate 52.45% over 1100 games matches the stored table; no elo-tier language present in either layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.trading still has no numbers, and nothing anywhere states the relationship between Apprehend's cooldown and Nasus's own Wither cooldown.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s; Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s. At rank 1 that is an eleven-second gap in Nasus's favour — after Darius burns the pull, Nasus's only defensive tool comes back well before Darius's only engage tool does. That is the concrete 'wait for X before you Y' the packet defect asks for, and it is why baiting Apprehend is worth taking chip damage for.
audit.corrected: After he burns Apprehend (26s at rank 1) your Wither (15s) is back long before his E is — that gap is the window to walk up and stack.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[0].t is 'Trade into his outer Q' but dontsFull[0].d never says what makes the outer Q different, so the entry tells the player to avoid something without telling them how.
audit.why: The mechanical answer is counter-intuitive: step in rather than out. Only Decimate's outer blade deals the bonus damage and heals Darius, so a melee stacker who is already standing next to him is safest staying there. Backing away is what walks you into the blade band.
audit.corrected: Put the blade/handle split into the .d text so the 'don't' carries its own fix.

audit.whatIsWrong: content whys[2] carries the third instance of the fabricated 'passive heal' claim, which the other two edits in this proposal remove from whys[0] and early.
audit.why: Leaving one instance in place is worse than leaving three, because the corrected strings around it will read as contradicting it. Hemorrhage is a bleed with a 5-stack AD enrage and no healing component of any kind.
audit.corrected: Replace the passive-heal clause with the real reason Spirit Fire poke loses: Decimate's blade heal outpaces it.

edits.after: Noxian Guillotine is true damage that scales with your bleed stacks — R's bonus armour does nothing, only the bonus HP does. Shed stacks first.

notes:
Darius's 'passive heal' appears three times in the content layer and is a fabricated mechanic — Hemorrhage has no healing component. Two further instances I could not fit inside the length band without gutting the surrounding advice: content whys[2] ('his bleed and passive heal beat your Spirit Fire poke'). Recommend a follow-up pass on that one string. Also note full-layer breakdown.cooldowns originally said Apprehend 'grants armor pen' on activation — the armour penetration is Apprehend's passive and is always on, not tied to the cast; the replacement text drops the claim rather than restating it.

SYSTEMIC, affects far more than this matchup: the full layer and the content layer carry two DIFFERENT level charts for every one of the nine matchups in this slice, disagreeing at one to five stages each. The full layer's stage-5 and stage-6 why-strings are boilerplate with the enemy name substituted in ('Sheen-item spike — Q now chunks a third of <enemy>'s HP...' and '300+ stacks and two items: you out-duel <enemy> on cooldown and three-shot his tower'), and phases[].side was frequently left at 'Skill' even where that same boilerplate says Nasus out-duels them. Worth deciding which array the front end actually reads — whichever it is, the other is unmaintained, and that divergence is what the packet's 'level chart contradicts data' defect is really detecting. I only proposed a side change where the full layer's own why text contradicted its own side field.

On the packet defect wording 'level chart contradicts data: Nasus wins 52.45% but the chart gives Darius 5/7 stages vs 1' — I deliberately did not flatten the early stages. Nasus genuinely loses levels 1-5 to Darius and wins the game on stacks; a lane chart that says so is correct, and rewriting it to track the headline win rate would make the site advise fights Nasus loses. The detector appears to assume chart share should follow win rate, which is wrong for hard-scaling champions as a class, not just here.

Unresolved and left alone deliberately: content whys[1] says 'Still no Wither and no ult' at level 2, whys[2] says 'You get Wither at 3', but full phases[1].why says 'Wither online' at level 2. The two layers assume different skill orders. Which is right is a build decision rather than a fact, so I changed neither — but someone who owns the recommended skill order should reconcile them, because right now the site tells the player both things.

Also flagging for any future edit: full report[8] (Itemization) contains a double space in 'Trinity Force  (Iceborn Gauntlet' that will break exact-match on that field.
